more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain fish roe.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: 0.16 mg boron/kg body weight/day, combined boric acid and borax (EFSA, 2013).
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA considered regular exceedance from assessed food uses unlikely.
Higher-dose animal studies found reproductive and developmental effects that supported the limit.
more_info.overview: Sodium tetraborate, also called borax, is an inorganic boron salt; the specified preparation is the hydrated form. Its preservative role is to limit spoilage caused by microorganisms and extend the storage life of the food. The specified material is supplied as powder or small sheets.
